_about: Mission blueprints (#641): how each master in masters/blueprints/ was made. The reference sheet is scripts/anatomy/blueprint-plan-view.ts <id>; the model (Higgsfield gpt_image_2_6, high, 4k, 3:2) redraws it by hand. Facts on each sheet are sourced below; after each sheet our own mission and fleet text is checked against it and fixed where it was wrong.
process: 1. Facts: dates, distances, launcher and spacecraft numbers from the sources listed; worked values from the site's Lab tools and ephemeris. Panel I is the MISSION BRIEF: four or five lines on why the mission matters, written from our own mission text (first / description) so the sheet and the site say the same.
2. Reference: npx tsx scripts/anatomy/blueprint-plan-view.ts <id> ref.png (computed plan view + panel layout), uploaded as the image reference.
3. Drafts: 1-2 at quality medium, 2k (1 credit each) to settle layout and wording.
4. Final: one render at quality high, 4k (4.25 credits), native 3504x2336 — no upscale needed (served base is 3072).
5. Fixes: local patches (glyphs copied from the same sheet, paper patches) or a small crop edit pasted back cell by cell.
6. Content check: our mission/fleet text vs the sheet; wrong numbers fixed in all 14 locales.

edits: spacecraft panel: the callout on the golden record read 5 (a second 5); replaced by the legend's own circled 6
v_esc formula: subscript ∞ in μ∞ redrawn as ☉

voyager-2.content_check: static/data/missions/neptune/voyager-2.json and the fleet entry: dates and distances agree with the sheet (Jupiter 721,670 km, Saturn 101,000 km, Uranus 81,500 km, Neptune 4,950 km above cloud tops, Triton ~40,000 km); no change needed.

From our mission text (first, description): 13 years, 294 orbits, 162 close moon flybys, Huygens 14 Jan 2005, Enceladus plumes, Titan lakes, end 15 Sep 2017 to protect Enceladus and Titan.
cassini.notes: The Venus 1 → Venus 2 leg is drawn as one conic; the real flight had a deep space manoeuvre on 3 Dec 1998, noted on the sheet. SRMU thrust left off: Wikipedia's 15.12 MN does not say per motor or both.
cassini.content_check: Fixed: our payload said the orbiter was ~5712 kg dry; 5,712 kg is the whole stack at launch, dry is 2,523 kg (all 14 locales, commit cd90ae7b4a5). Checked and kept: Huygens ~318 kg (ESA probe mass), Venus 1 284 km (JPL); the sheet uses these. Added to the sheet from our data: SOI 96-minute burn, 626 m/s (JPL).

queue._about: Order for the remaining /explore missions (2026-11-06): the most distinct missions first, near-twins of a sheet already done (or of one earlier in the list) last. 'needs' = what blueprint-plan-view.ts lacks for that mission today.

order.why: comet chase: three Earth flybys and one of Mars, ten years to rendezvous, orbit and Philae lander
out of the ecliptic: Jupiter flings it over the Sun’s poles — the side elevation becomes the hero
fastest launch ever, one Jupiter assist, Pluto and then Arrokoth
Venus lander: a short transfer inward, 127 minutes on a 457 °C surface, first colour images
order.needs: inward transfer; entry/landing in place of flybys

order.why: VEEGA path, Jupiter orbiter and the first probe into a giant planet’s atmosphere
ion engine: orbited two bodies, Vesta then Ceres
round trip: ion engine to Ryugu, sample, return capsule to Earth
solar-powered polar orbiter of Jupiter after one Earth flyby
nine flybys (Earth, Venus ×2, Mercury ×6) to brake into Mercury orbit
order.needs: Mercury in the ephemeris types, many short legs

order.why: first lunar–Earth double flyby, to end in Ganymede orbit
order.needs: Moon flyby in the inner detail; future events marked planned

order.why: closest look at Halley’s nucleus, 596 km, then Grigg–Skjellerup
first through the asteroid belt and first to Jupiter
Venus balloon and lander, then Halley — close to Venera 13 and Giotto
Pioneer 10’s twin, on to Saturn — close to Pioneer 10
Voyager 2’s twin: Jupiter, Saturn, Titan and out — close to Voyager 2
Vega 1’s twin — the last, most similar sheet
